passages.text: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” “Here I am,” Esau replied.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was old.
Isaac could not see well.
Isaac’s eyes were weak.
Isaac called Esau.
Esau was Isaac’s older son.
Isaac said to Esau, “My son.”
Esau answered Isaac.
Esau said, “Here I am.”
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ כִּֽי־ זָקֵ֣ן יִצְחָ֔ק וַתִּכְהֶ֥יןָ עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְאֹ֑ת וַיִּקְרָ֞א אֶת־ עֵשָׂ֣ו׀ בְּנ֣וֹ הַגָּדֹ֗ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ בְּנִ֔י וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: “Look,” said Isaac, “I am now old, and I do not know the day of my death.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was old.
Isaac spoke.
Isaac said, “Look at me.
I am now old.
I do not know the day I will die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־ נָ֖א זָקַ֑נְתִּי לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי י֥וֹם מוֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: Take your weapons—your quiver and bow—and go out into the field to hunt some game for me.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was old and could not see.
Isaac spoke to Esau, his older son.
Isaac said, “Take your weapons.
Take your quiver.
Take your bow.
Go out into the field.
Hunt some game for me.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ שָׂא־ נָ֣א כֵלֶ֔יךָ תֶּלְיְךָ֖ וְקַשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְצֵא֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְצ֥וּדָה לִּ֖י צֵידָה׃

passages.text: Then prepare a tasty dish that I love and bring it to me to eat, so that I may bless you before I die.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was old and did not know when he would die.
Isaac spoke to his son Esau.
Isaac said, "Prepare a tasty dish that I love.
Bring it to me.
I will eat it.
Then I will bless you before I die."
passages.original: וַעֲשֵׂה־ לִ֨י מַטְעַמִּ֜ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהַ֛בְתִּי וְהָבִ֥יאָה לִּ֖י וְאֹכֵ֑לָה בַּעֲב֛וּר תְּבָרֶכְךָ֥ נַפְשִׁ֖י בְּטֶ֥רֶם אָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Now Rebekah was listening to what Isaac told his son Esau. So when Esau went into the field to hunt game and bring it back, Rebekah said to her son Jacob, “Behold, I overheard your father saying to your brother Esau, ‘Bring me some game and prepare me a tasty dish to eat, so that I may bless you in the presence of the LORD before I die.’
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was Isaac’s wife.
Isaac spoke to his son Esau.
Rebekah listened to Isaac’s words.
Esau was Isaac’s older son.
Esau went out into the field.
Esau went to hunt game and bring it back.
Rebekah spoke to her son Jacob.
Jacob was Rebekah’s younger son.
Rebekah said, “I heard your father speaking to your brother Esau.”
Rebekah repeated Isaac’s words.
Isaac said, “Bring me some game.”
Isaac said, “Prepare a tasty dish for me to eat.”
Isaac said, “I will bless you in the presence of the LORD before I die.”
passages.original: וְרִבְקָ֣ה שֹׁמַ֔עַת בְּדַבֵּ֣ר יִצְחָ֔ק אֶל־ עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ עֵשָׂו֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לָצ֥וּד צַ֖יִד לְהָבִֽיא׃ וְרִבְקָה֙ אָֽמְרָ֔ה אֶל־ יַעֲקֹ֥ב בְּנָ֖הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֤ה שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־ אָבִ֔יךָ מְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶל־ עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יךָ לֵאמֹֽר׃ הָבִ֨יאָה לִּ֥י צַ֛יִד וַעֲשֵׂה־ לִ֥י מַטְעַמִּ֖ים וְאֹכֵ֑לָה וַאֲבָרֶכְכָ֛ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: Now, my son, listen to my voice and do exactly as I tell you.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah spoke to her son Jacob.
She said, "My son, listen to me."
Do what I command you.
Follow my instructions exactly.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֥ה בְנִ֖י שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֑י לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י מְצַוָּ֥ה אֹתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I can make them into a tasty dish for your father—the kind he loves.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah spoke to her son Jacob.
She gave him instructions.
She said, "Go to the flock."
"Bring me two good young goats."
"I will prepare them as a tasty dish."
"This dish is for your father."
"He loves this kind of food."
passages.original: לֶךְ־ נָא֙ אֶל־ הַצֹּ֔אן וְקַֽח־ לִ֣י מִשָּׁ֗ם שְׁנֵ֛י גְּדָיֵ֥י עִזִּ֖ים טֹבִ֑ים וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֨ה אֹתָ֧ם מַטְעַמִּ֛ים לְאָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהֵֽב׃

passages.text: Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was Rebekah’s son.
Rebekah spoke to Jacob.
She told Jacob to bring the food to his father.
Jacob’s father was Isaac.
Isaac was old and near death.
Rebekah wanted Isaac to eat the food.
She wanted Isaac to bless Jacob before Isaac died.
passages.original: וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ לְאָבִ֖יךָ וְאָכָ֑ל בַּעֲבֻ֛ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְבָרֶכְךָ֖ לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, but I am smooth-skinned.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to his mother Rebekah.
Jacob said, “Esau is my brother.
Esau is a hairy man.
I am not like Esau.
I have smooth skin.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל־ רִבְקָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ הֵ֣ן עֵשָׂ֤ו אָחִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ שָׂעִ֔ר וְאָנֹכִ֖י אִ֥ישׁ חָלָֽק׃

passages.text: What if my father touches me? Then I would be revealed to him as a deceiver, and I would bring upon myself a curse rather than a blessing.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the younger son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob spoke to his mother, Rebekah.
Jacob said, “What if my father touches me?
My father is Isaac.
He might feel my skin.
He might notice I am not Esau.
He might see that I am trying to deceive him.
He might think I am a trickster.
If that happens, I will bring a curse on myself.
I will not receive a blessing.”
passages.original: אוּלַ֤י יְמֻשֵּׁ֙נִי֙ אָבִ֔י וְהָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָ֖יו כִּמְתַעְתֵּ֑עַ וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י עָלַ֛י קְלָלָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א בְרָכָֽה׃

passages.text: His mother replied, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just obey my voice and go get them for me.”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was Jacob’s mother.
Rebekah spoke to Jacob.
Rebekah said, “If there is a curse, let it fall on me, my son.”
Rebekah said, “Listen to my voice.”
Rebekah said, “Go and get the goats for me.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִמּ֔וֹ עָלַ֥י קִלְלָתְךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י אַ֛ךְ שְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹלִ֖י וְלֵ֥ךְ קַֽח־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: So Jacob went and got two goats and brought them to his mother, who made the tasty food his father loved.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the younger son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Jacob obeyed his mother Rebekah.
Jacob went out.
Jacob got two goats.
Jacob brought the goats to his mother Rebekah.
Rebekah was Jacob’s mother.
Rebekah prepared tasty food.
Rebekah made the food the way Isaac, her husband, loved.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיִּקַּ֔ח וַיָּבֵ֖א לְאִמּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֤עַשׂ אִמּוֹ֙ מַטְעַמִּ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָהֵ֥ב אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: And Rebekah took the finest clothes in the house that belonged to her older son Esau, and she put them on her younger son Jacob.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was the mother of Esau and Jacob.
Esau was her older son.
Jacob was her younger son.
Rebekah took Esau’s best clothes.
These clothes were in her house.
She put Esau’s clothes on Jacob.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֣ח רִ֠בְקָה אֶת־ בִּגְדֵ֨י עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּנָ֤הּ הַגָּדֹל֙ הַחֲמֻדֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתָּ֖הּ בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתַּלְבֵּ֥שׁ אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּנָ֥הּ הַקָּטָֽן׃

passages.text: She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was Jacob’s mother.
She took the skins of the young goats.
She put the skins on Jacob’s hands.
She put the skins on the smooth part of Jacob’s neck.
passages.original: וְאֵ֗ת עֹרֹת֙ גְּדָיֵ֣י הָֽעִזִּ֔ים הִלְבִּ֖ישָׁה עַל־ יָדָ֑יו וְעַ֖ל חֶלְקַ֥ת צַוָּארָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and bread she had made.
passages.sermon: Rebekah was the mother of Jacob.\r\nRebekah made tasty food and bread.\r\nRebekah gave the food and bread to her son Jacob.
passages.original: וַתִּתֵּ֧ן אֶת־ הַמַּטְעַמִּ֛ים וְאֶת־ הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑תָה בְּיַ֖ד יַעֲקֹ֥ב בְּנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: So Jacob went to his father and said, “My father.” “Here I am!” he answered. “Which one are you, my son?”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the younger son of Isaac.
Isaac was old and could not see well.
Jacob went to his father Isaac.
Jacob spoke to his father.
Jacob said, “My father.”
Isaac answered Jacob.
Isaac said, “Here I am!”
Isaac asked Jacob a question.
Isaac said, “Which one are you, my son?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֶל־ אָבִ֖יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הִנֶּ֔נִּי מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה בְּנִֽי׃

passages.text: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to his father Isaac.
Jacob said, “I am Esau, your firstborn son.”
Jacob said, “I did what you told me.”
Jacob said, “Please sit up.”
Jacob said, “Eat some of my game.”
Jacob said, “Then your soul may bless me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶל־ אָבִ֗יו אָנֹכִי֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו בְּכֹרֶ֔ךָ עָשִׂ֕יתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ אֵלָ֑י קֽוּם־ נָ֣א שְׁבָ֗ה וְאָכְלָה֙ מִצֵּידִ֔י בַּעֲב֖וּר תְּבָרֲכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: But Isaac asked his son, “How did you ever find it so quickly, my son?” “Because the LORD your God brought it to me,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Jacob’s father.
Isaac spoke to his son.
Isaac asked, “How did you find it so quickly, my son?”
Jacob answered Isaac.
Jacob said, “The LORD your God brought it to me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶל־ בְּנ֔וֹ מַה־ זֶּ֛ה מִהַ֥רְתָּ לִמְצֹ֖א בְּנִ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י הִקְרָ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְפָנָֽי׃

passages.text: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come closer so I can touch you, my son. Are you really my son Esau, or not?”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Jacob’s father.
Isaac spoke to Jacob.
Isaac said, “Come closer, my son.”
Isaac said, “I want to touch you.”
Isaac said, “Are you really my son Esau?”
Isaac asked, “Or are you not?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹ֔ב גְּשָׁה־ נָּ֥א וַאֲמֻֽשְׁךָ֖ בְּנִ֑י הַֽאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֛ה בְּנִ֥י עֵשָׂ֖ו אִם־ לֹֽא׃

passages.text: So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the younger son of Isaac.
Isaac was old and could not see well.
Jacob came close to his father Isaac.
Isaac touched Jacob.
Isaac listened to Jacob’s voice.
Isaac said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob.”
Isaac felt Jacob’s hands.
Isaac said, “The hands are the hands of Esau.”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֧שׁ יַעֲקֹ֛ב אֶל־ יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו וַיְמֻשֵּׁ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַקֹּל֙ ק֣וֹל יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְהַיָּדַ֖יִם יְדֵ֥י עֵשָֽׂו׃

passages.text: Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Jacob and Esau.
Isaac could not recognize Jacob.
Jacob’s hands felt hairy.
Esau, Jacob’s brother, had hairy hands.
Isaac felt Jacob’s hands.
Isaac thought the hands were like Esau’s hands.
Isaac did not realize it was Jacob.
Isaac blessed Jacob.
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א הִכִּיר֔וֹ כִּֽי־ הָי֣וּ יָדָ֗יו כִּידֵ֛י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִ֖יו שְׂעִרֹ֑ת וַֽיְבָרְכֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Again he asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he replied, “I am.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Jacob’s father.
Isaac could not see well.
Isaac asked Jacob a question.
Isaac said, “Are you really my son Esau?”
Jacob answered Isaac.
Jacob said, “I am.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י עֵשָׂ֑ו וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: “Serve me,” said Isaac, “and let me eat some of my son’s game, so that I may bless you.” Jacob brought it to him, and he ate; then he brought him wine, and he drank.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Jacob and Esau.
Isaac spoke to Jacob.
Isaac said, “Bring me some of your game, my son.
Let me eat it.
Then my soul will bless you.”
Jacob brought the food to Isaac.
Isaac ate the food.
Jacob also brought wine to Isaac.
Isaac drank the wine.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הַגִּ֤שָׁה לִּי֙ וְאֹֽכְלָה֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנִ֔י לְמַ֥עַן תְּבָֽרֶכְךָ֖ נַפְשִׁ֑י וַיַּגֶּשׁ־ לוֹ֙ וַיֹּאכַ֔ל וַיָּ֧בֵא ל֦וֹ יַ֖יִן וַיֵּֽשְׁתְּ׃

passages.text: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Jacob’s father.
Isaac spoke to Jacob.
Isaac said, “Come near to me, my son.”
Isaac said, “Kiss me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֑יו גְּשָׁה־ נָּ֥א וּשְׁקָה־ לִּ֖י בְּנִֽי׃

passages.text: So he came near and kissed him. When Isaac smelled his clothing, he blessed him and said: “Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Jacob’s father.
Isaac could not see well.
Jacob came close to Isaac.
Jacob kissed Isaac.
Isaac smelled Jacob’s clothes.
Isaac noticed the smell of the clothes.
Isaac blessed Jacob.
Isaac said, “Look, my son smells like a field.”
Isaac said, “The LORD has blessed this field.”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ וַיִּשַּׁק־ ל֔וֹ וַיָּ֛רַח אֶת־ רֵ֥יחַ בְּגָדָ֖יו וַֽיְבָרֲכֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רְאֵה֙ רֵ֣יחַ בְּנִ֔י כְּרֵ֣יחַ שָׂדֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּרֲכ֖וֹ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: May God give to you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth— an abundance of grain and new wine.
passages.sermon:
Isaac is the father of Jacob.
Isaac speaks to Jacob.
Isaac blesses Jacob.
Isaac says, “May God give you good things.”
May God give you dew from heaven.
May God give you the richness of the earth.
May God give you much grain.
May God give you much new wine.
passages.original: וְיִֽתֶּן־ לְךָ֙ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מִטַּל֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּמִשְׁמַנֵּ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹ֥ב דָּגָ֖ן וְתִירֹֽשׁ׃

passages.text: May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. May you be the master of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Jacob and Esau.
Isaac spoke to Jacob.
Isaac gave Jacob a blessing.
Isaac said, “Peoples will serve you.
Nations will bow down to you.
You will be the master over your brothers.
The sons of your mother will bow down to you.
Anyone who curses you will be cursed.
Anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
passages.original: יַֽעַבְד֣וּךָ עַמִּ֗ים וְיִשְׁתַּחוּ לְךָ֙ לְאֻמִּ֔ים הֱוֵ֤ה גְבִיר֙ לְאַחֶ֔יךָ וְיִשְׁתַּחֲוּ֥וּ לְךָ֖ בְּנֵ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ אֹרְרֶ֣יךָ אָר֔וּר וּֽמְבָרֲכֶ֖יךָ בָּרֽוּךְ׃

passages.text: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing him and Jacob had left his father’s presence, his brother Esau returned from the hunt.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Jacob and Esau.
Isaac finished blessing Jacob.
Jacob left Isaac’s presence.
Esau was Jacob’s brother.
Esau returned from hunting.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר כִּלָּ֣ה יִצְחָק֮ לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹב֒ וַיְהִ֗י אַ֣ךְ יָצֹ֤א יָצָא֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב מֵאֵ֥ת פְּנֵ֖י יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֑יו וְעֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֔יו בָּ֖א מִצֵּידֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He too made some tasty food, brought it to his father, and said to him, “My father, sit up and eat of your son’s game, so that you may bless me.”
passages.sermon:
Esau was Isaac’s son and Jacob’s brother.
Esau also prepared tasty food.
Esau brought the food to his father Isaac.
Esau spoke to his father Isaac.
Esau said, “My father, sit up and eat the game I hunted.
Eat it so that your soul may bless me.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ גַּם־ הוּא֙ מַטְעַמִּ֔ים וַיָּבֵ֖א לְאָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֗יו יָקֻ֤ם אָבִי֙ וְיֹאכַל֙ מִצֵּ֣יד בְּנ֔וֹ בַּעֲב֖וּר תְּבָרֲכַ֥נִּי נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: But his father Isaac replied, “Who are you?” “I am Esau, your firstborn son,” he answered.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob.
Isaac spoke to the man before him.
Isaac asked, "Who are you?"
The man answered Isaac.
He said, "I am Esau."
He said, "I am your firstborn son."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֛וֹ יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו מִי־ אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֲנִ֛י בִּנְךָ֥ בְכֹֽרְךָ֖ עֵשָֽׂו׃

passages.text: Isaac began to tremble violently and said, “Who was it, then, who hunted the game and brought it to me? Before you came in, I ate it all and blessed him—and indeed, he will be blessed!”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob.
Isaac realized something was wrong.
Isaac began to tremble very greatly.
Isaac said, "Who was it who hunted game and brought it to me?"
Isaac said, "I ate all of it before you came in."
Isaac said, "I blessed him."
Isaac said, "He will surely be blessed."
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱרַ֨ד יִצְחָ֣ק חֲרָדָה֮ גְּדֹלָ֣ה עַד־ מְאֹד֒ וַיֹּ֡אמֶר מִֽי־ אֵפ֡וֹא ה֣וּא הַצָּֽד־ צַיִד֩ וַיָּ֨בֵא לִ֜י וָאֹכַ֥ל מִכֹּ֛ל בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא וָאֲבָרֲכֵ֑הוּ גַּם־ בָּר֖וּךְ יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me too, O my father!”
passages.sermon:
Esau was Isaac’s son.
Isaac spoke words to Esau.
Esau heard his father’s words.
Esau cried out loudly.
His cry was very great and bitter.
Esau said to his father, “Bless me too, my father.”
passages.original: כִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ עֵשָׂו֙ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו וַיִּצְעַ֣ק צְעָקָ֔ה גְּדֹלָ֥ה וּמָרָ֖ה עַד־ מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְאָבִ֔יו בָּרֲכֵ֥נִי גַם־ אָ֖נִי אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: But Isaac replied, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Esau’s father.
Isaac spoke to Esau.
Isaac said, “Your brother came in secret.
He acted with deceit.
He took your blessing.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בָּ֥א אָחִ֖יךָ בְּמִרְמָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֖ח בִּרְכָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So Esau declared, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me twice. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” Then he asked, “Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?”
passages.sermon:
Esau spoke to his father Isaac.
Esau said, “Jacob is the right name for my brother.”
Jacob means ‘he deceives’ or ‘he cheats.’
Jacob has deceived me two times.
First, Jacob took my birthright.
Now, Jacob has taken my blessing.”
Esau asked Isaac, “Have you saved a blessing for me?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר הֲכִי֩ קָרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַֽיַּעְקְבֵ֙נִי֙ זֶ֣ה פַעֲמַ֔יִם אֶת־ בְּכֹרָתִ֣י לָקָ֔ח וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַתָּ֖ה לָקַ֣ח בִּרְכָתִ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר הֲלֹא־ אָצַ֥לְתָּ לִּ֖י בְּרָכָֽה׃

passages.text: But Isaac answered Esau: “Look, I have made him your master and given him all his relatives as servants; I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What is left that I can do for you, my son?”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Esau’s father.
Isaac spoke to Esau.
Isaac said, “I have made your brother your master.
I have given all his relatives to him as servants.
I have supported him with grain.
I have supported him with new wine.
My son, what can I do for you now?”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן יִצְחָ֜ק וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֵשָׂ֗ו הֵ֣ן גְּבִ֞יר שַׂמְתִּ֥יו לָךְ֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ אֶחָ֗יו נָתַ֤תִּי לוֹ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים וְדָגָ֥ן וְתִירֹ֖שׁ סְמַכְתִּ֑יו וּלְכָ֣ה אֵפ֔וֹא מָ֥ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה בְּנִֽי׃

passages.text: Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, O my father!” Then Esau wept aloud.
passages.sermon:
Esau was Isaac’s older son.
Esau spoke to his father Isaac.
Esau asked, “Do you have only one blessing, my father?”
Esau said, “Bless me also, my father.”
Esau raised his voice.
Esau wept.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו אֶל־ אָבִ֗יו הַֽבְרָכָ֨ה אַחַ֤ת הִֽוא־ לְךָ֙ אָבִ֔י בָּרֲכֵ֥נִי גַם־ אָ֖נִי אָבִ֑י וַיִּשָּׂ֥א עֵשָׂ֛ו קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ׃

passages.text: His father Isaac answered him: “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Esau’s father.
Isaac spoke to Esau.
Isaac said, “Look, you will live far from the rich places of the earth.
You will live far from the dew that comes from heaven above.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֛עַן יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו הִנֵּ֞ה מִשְׁמַנֵּ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה מֽוֹשָׁבֶ֔ךָ וּמִטַּ֥ל הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מֵעָֽל׃

passages.text: You shall live by the sword and serve your brother. But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac spoke to Esau.
Isaac was Esau’s father.
Isaac said, “You will live by your sword.
You will serve your brother Jacob.
But one day you will grow restless.
Then you will break free from your brother’s control.
You will remove his yoke from your neck.”
passages.original: וְעַל־ חַרְבְּךָ֣ תִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְאֶת־ אָחִ֖יךָ תַּעֲבֹ֑ד וְהָיָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּרִ֔יד וּפָרַקְתָּ֥ עֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֥ל צַוָּארֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
passages.sermon:
Esau was Isaac’s older son.
Jacob was Isaac’s younger son.
Isaac gave Jacob a blessing.
Esau’s father gave this blessing to Jacob.
Esau felt anger toward Jacob because of this blessing.
Esau held a grudge against Jacob.
Esau thought to himself.
He said in his heart, “Soon my father will die.”
He said, “When the days of mourning for my father come, I will kill my brother Jacob.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂטֹ֤ם עֵשָׂו֙ אֶֽת־ יַעֲקֹ֔ב עַל־ הַ֨בְּרָכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּרֲכ֖וֹ אָבִ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר עֵשָׂ֜ו בְּלִבּ֗וֹ יִקְרְבוּ֙ יְמֵי֙ אֵ֣בֶל אָבִ֔י וְאַֽהַרְגָ֖ה אֶת־ יַעֲקֹ֥ב אָחִֽי׃

passages.text: When the words of her older son Esau were relayed to Rebekah, she sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Look, your brother Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was the mother of Esau and Jacob.
Esau was her older son.
Jacob was her younger son.
Someone told Rebekah what Esau had said.
Rebekah sent for Jacob.
Rebekah called Jacob, her younger son.
Rebekah spoke to Jacob.
She said, “Look, your brother Esau is planning to kill you to comfort himself.”
passages.original: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְרִבְקָ֔ה אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֥י עֵשָׂ֖ו בְּנָ֣הּ הַגָּדֹ֑ל וַתִּשְׁלַ֞ח וַתִּקְרָ֤א לְיַעֲקֹב֙ בְּנָ֣הּ הַקָּטָ֔ן וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּה֙ עֵשָׂ֣ו אָחִ֔יךָ מִתְנַחֵ֥ם לְךָ֖ לְהָרְגֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.
passages.sermon:
Rebekah was Jacob’s mother.
Rebekah spoke to Jacob.
Rebekah said, “My son, listen to me.”
Rebekah told Jacob to obey her.
Rebekah said, “Get up and run away.”
Rebekah told Jacob to go to her brother Laban.
Laban lived in Haran.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֥ה בְנִ֖י שְׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֑י וְק֧וּם בְּרַח־ לְךָ֛ אֶל־ לָבָ֥ן אָחִ֖י חָרָֽנָה׃

passages.text: Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides— until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah spoke to Jacob, her younger son.
She told him to stay with Laban, her brother.
She said, “Stay with him for a while.
Wait until your brother Esau’s anger passes.
Wait until Esau’s rage against you fades.
Wait until Esau forgets what you did to him.
Then I will send for you.
I will bring you back from there.
I do not want to lose both of you in one day.”
passages.original: וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֥ עִמּ֖וֹ יָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֑ים עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־ תָּשׁ֖וּב חֲמַ֥ת אָחִֽיךָ׃ עַד־ שׁ֨וּב אַף־ אָחִ֜יךָ מִמְּךָ֗ וְשָׁכַח֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֖י וּלְקַחְתִּ֣יךָ מִשָּׁ֑ם לָמָ֥ה אֶשְׁכַּ֛ל גַּם־ שְׁנֵיכֶ֖ם י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”
passages.sermon:
Rebekah spoke to Isaac.
Rebekah was Isaac’s wife.
Rebekah said she was weary of her life.
Rebekah said the Hittite women caused her distress.
Rebekah said, “If Jacob marries a Hittite woman from this land, my life will have no value to me.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רִבְקָה֙ אֶל־ יִצְחָ֔ק קַ֣צְתִּי בְחַיַּ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנ֣וֹת חֵ֑ת אִם־ לֹקֵ֣חַ יַ֠עֲקֹב אִשָּׁ֨ה מִבְּנֽוֹת־ חֵ֤ת כָּאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִבְּנ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ לָ֥מָּה לִּ֖י חַיִּֽים׃
